Section 2 777 Dispatch Deviations Guide ATA 21
21-00-01 Environmental Control System Miscellaneous Cards
(ECSMC)
21-00-01-01 Passenger
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 2 1 (M) (O)
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated ECSMC is deactivated.
b. Both ARINC Signal Gateway cards in the opposite cardfile operate normally.
c. Opposite equipment cooling controller operates normally.
d. Opposite equipment cooling supply fan operates normally.
e. Opposite lavatory/galley fan operates normally.
f. One pack operates normally.
g. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
For FCAC installed:
h. For right ECSMC inoperative, FCAC remains OFF.
MAINTENANCE (M)
NOTE: For a pack to be operating normally, certain items associated with that
system must be operative. See DDG item 21-51-01 for a listing of those
items.
Deactivate the inoperative ECSMC and for Forward Cargo Air Conditioning
installed with right ECSMC inoperative, position FWD CARGO A/C control OFF
(AMM 21-00-00/901).
1. Deactivate the inoperative ECSMC (AMM 21-00-00/901).
NOTE 1:For left ECSMC deactivated: The left lower and forward upper
recirculation fans are inoperative and also considered
deactivated. The RECIRC FAN status message will be displayed.
The aft cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT AFT
advisory message will be displayed.
NOTE 2:For right ECSMC deactivated: The right lower and aft upper
recirculation fans are inoperative and also considered
deactivated. The RECIRC FAN status message will be displayed.
The bulk cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT BULK
advisory message will be displayed.
A. Gain access to the right systems cardfile (P84) or left systems cardfile
(P85) in the main equipment center.
B. Set the power switch for the inoperative ECSMC to the OFF position.

2. For right ECSMC inoperative, position Overhead Panel (P5) FWD CARGO

OPERATIONS (O)
1. For left ECSMC deactivated:
A. Aft cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT AFT advisory
message will be displayed.
B. Use DDG item 21-44-01 (O) Note for predicting aft cargo
compartment temperatures. Temperature sensitive cargo should not
be carried in the aft cargo compartment.
NOTE: Actual aft cargo compartment temperature will not be
available on the Air Synoptic.
C. Left lower and forward upper recirculation fans are inoperative.
Increase flight planning fuel by 0.7%.
2. For right ECSMC deactivated:
A. Bulk cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT BULK advisory
message will be displayed.
B. Use DDG item 21-44-03 (O) Note for predicting bulk cargo
compartment temperatures. Temperature sensitive cargo should not
be carried in the bulk cargo compartment.
NOTE: Actual bulk cargo compartment temperature will not be
available on the Air Synoptic.
C. Right lower and aft upper recirculation fans are inoperative. Increase
flight planning fuel by 0.7%.
For Forward Cargo Air Conditioning (FCAC) installed:
D. FCAC is inoperative and must remain OFF. Temperature sensitive
cargo should not be carried in the forward cargo compartment.

21-25-01 Recirculation Fans
21-25-01-01 Passenger
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 4 0 (M) (O)
May be inoperative provided associated recirculation fan is deactivated.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the inoperative recirculation fan (AMM 21-00-00/901).
NOTE: The RECIRC FAN status message indicates one or more fans are
inoperative.
1. Determine which recirculation fan is inoperative:
A. Position both Air Conditioning Panel (P5) PACK switches to OFF.
B. Position both Air Conditioning Panel (P5) RECIRC FANS switches to
ON.
C. On the Air Conditioning Maintenance page, use the recirculation fan
status to determine the inoperative fan.
D. Position both Air Conditioning Panel (P5) PACK switches to AUTO.
2. Deactivate the inoperative recirculation fan.
A. For forward upper recirculation fan inoperative, open and collar the
P110 panel FWD UPR RECIRC FAN circuit breaker.
B. For aft upper recirculation fan inoperative, open and collar the P210
panel AFT UPR RECIRC FAN circuit breaker.
C. For left lower recirculation fan inoperative, open and collar the P110
panel L LWR RECIRC FAN circuit breaker.
For -200/-200ER/-200LR airplanes without Forward Cargo Air
Conditioning (FCAC) installed:
D. For right lower recirculation fan inoperative, open and collar the P210
panel R LWR RECIRC FAN circuit breaker.
For -200/-200ER/-200LR airplanes with Forward Cargo Air Conditioning
(FCAC) installed, and for -300/-300ER airplanes:
E. For right lower recirculation fan inoperative:
1) Open the P210 panel AFT UPR/R LWR RECIRC FAN CTRL
circuit breaker.
2) Gain access to the lower recirculation fans by removing the aft
endwall in the forward cargo compartment.
3) Disconnect, cap and stow the electrical connector (DB21252)
from the right lower recirculation fan.
4) Re-install the endwall.
Boeing Proprietary. Copyright ©Boeing. ECCN: 9E991. See title page for details.

5) Close the P210 panel AFT UPR/R LWR RECIRC FAN CTRL
circuit breaker.
OPERATIONS (O)
Fuel penalties are negligible with one recirculation fan inoperative. For two
recirculation fans inoperative, increase flight planning fuel by 0.7%, plus 0.3% for
each additional inoperative fan.
For Forward Cargo Air Conditioning (FCAC) installed:
NOTE: For one or both lower recirculation fans inoperative, temperature
control in the forward cargo compartment may be degraded.

ATA 21 777 Dispatch Deviations Guide Section 2
21-26-01 Lavatory/Galley Ventilation Fans
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 2 1 (M)
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative ventilation fan is deactivated.
b. Opposite ECSMC operates normally.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the inoperative lavatory/galley ventilation fan (AMM 21-00-00/901).
1. For the left lavatory/galley ventilation fan inoperative:
NOTE: The right ECSMC must operate normally.
A. Open and collar the P110 panel L LAV/GLY FAN CTRL circuit
breaker.
B. For P110 panel L LAV/GLY FAN circuit breaker installed, open and
collar the circuit breaker.
C. For P110 panel L LAV/GLY FAN circuit breaker not installed:
1) Gain access to the left lavatory/galley ventilation fan by
removing the left endwall in the bulk cargo compartment.
2) Disconnect, cap and stow the electrical connector (DB21262)
from the left lavatory/galley ventilation fan.
3) Re-install the endwall.
2. For the right lavatory/galley ventilation fan inoperative:
NOTE: The left ECSMC must operate normally.
A. Open and collar the P210 panel R LAV/GLY FAN CTRL circuit
breaker.
B. For P210 panel R LAV/GLY FAN circuit breaker installed, open and
collar the circuit breaker.
C. For P210 panel R LAV/GLY FAN circuit breaker not installed:
1) Gain access to the right lavatory/galley ventilation fan by
removing the left endwall in the bulk cargo compartment.
2) Disconnect, cap and stow the electrical connector (DB21261)
from the right lavatory/galley ventilation fan.
3) Re-install the endwall.

21-26-04 Cabin Smoking Area Ventilation Exhaust Valves
***
Interval Installed Required Procedure
D - 0 (M)
May be inoperative provided the inoperative exhaust valve(s) is deactivated
closed.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the inoperative cabin smoking area ventilation exhaust valve closed
(AMM 21-00-00/901).
1. For the aft ventilation exhaust valve inoperative:
A. Open and collar P110 panel circuit breaker AFT CABIN EXHAUST
VALVE.
B. Gain access to the aft exhaust valve located in the crown above the
ceiling panels near Door 4R at STA 1954, WL 326, RBL 27 by
removing the ceiling panels and moisture shroud.
C. Manually position the aft exhaust valve closed.
D. Re-install ceiling panels and moisture shroud.
2. For the forward ventilation exhaust valve inoperative:
A. Open and collar P110 panel circuit breaker FWD CABIN EXHAUST
VALVE.
B. Gain access to the forward exhaust valve located in the crown above
the ceiling panels near Door 2R at STA 739, WL 318, RBL 51 by
removing the ceiling panels and moisture shroud.
C. Manually position the forward exhaust valve closed.
D. Re-install ceiling panels and moisture shroud.

Interval Installed Required Procedure

1. Open and collar P110 panel FWD CGO EXHAUST FAN CTRL circuit

***

21-27-02 Equipment Cooling Supply Fans
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 2 1 (M)
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative supply fan is deactivated.
b. Opposite ECSMC operates normally.
c. Both override valve motors operate normally.
d. Both equipment cooling controllers operate normally.
e. Flight is conducted pressurized.
MAINTENANCE (M)
NOTE 1:At least one pack and two engine bleed systems must operate normally,
or both packs and at least one engine bleed system must operate
normally.
NOTE 2:For a pack to be operating normally, certain items associated with that
system must be operative. See DDG item 21-51-01 for a listing of those
items.
NOTE 3:For an engine bleed system to be operating normally, certain items
associated with that system must be operative. See DDG item 36-00-01
for a listing of those items.
NOTE 4:Dispatch is not allowed using the unpressurized dispatch option for
MMEL items: 21-31-01, 21-31-02, 21-31-03, 21-31-05, 21-31-06,
21-31-07, 21-32-01, 21-32-02, and 21-61-01.
Deactivate the inoperative equipment cooling supply fan (AMM 21-00-00/901).
1. For the left equipment cooling supply fan inoperative:
A. Open and collar the P110 panel EQPT CLG SPLY FAN 1 CTRL
circuit breaker.
B. Gain access to the left equipment cooling supply fan located in the
lower forward cargo compartment behind the left sidewall panel near
the forward ball panel.
C. Disconnect, cap and stow the electrical connector (DB21581) from
the left equipment cooling supply fan.

22-11-01 Autopilot Flight Director Computers (AFDC)
22-11-01A One Inoperative
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 3 2 (M) (O)
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated AFDC is deactivated.
b. Associated AFDC backdrive actuator is deactivated.
c. Approach minimums do not require use of the associated autopilot.
MAINTENANCE (M)
NOTE: The AFDCs are interchangeable. The failed AFDC may be moved to the
center position to maintain left and right backdrive functions operational.
Deactivate the inoperative AFDC and associated backdrive actuator (AMM
22-00-00/901).
1. For the center AFDC inoperative, open and collar the P11 panel AFDC C
circuit breaker.
2. For the left AFDC inoperative:
A. Open and collar the P11 panel AFDC L circuit breaker.
B. Open and collar the P11 panel AFDC BACK DRIVE L circuit breaker.
3. For the right AFDC inoperative:
A. Open and collar the P11 panel AFDC R circuit breaker.
B. Open and collar the P11 panel AFDC BACK DRIVE R circuit breaker.
OPERATIONS (O)
1. Align the ADIRU.
2. For the left or right AFDC inoperative, confirm the autopilot system is
operational by engaging and disengaging the autopilot on the ground with
flaps UP before each departure.
3. The autoland system is not fail-operational and the NO LAND 3 advisory
message will be displayed.

MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the associated autothrottle servo motor (AMM 22-00-00/901).
1. For the left A/T ARM switch inoperative, open and collar P11 panel A/T
SERVO L circuit breaker.
2. For the right A/T ARM switch inoperative, open and collar P11 panel A/T
SERVO R circuit breaker.
OPERATIONS (O)
1. The AUTOTHROTTLE L or R advisory message will be displayed.
2. The autothrottle cannot be engaged on the ground.
3. Set both thrust levers manually for takeoff and go-around.
4. The flight must remain within 180 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
5. For an inoperative switch failed to the armed state, the EPR trim function
will operate normally, provided the operative autothrottle arm switch is
positioned to A/T ARM.
NOTE: The autothrottle disconnect caution will be annunciated if the flight
crew selects FLCH, VNAV, or TO/GA. Pressing the autothrottle
disconnect switch will clear the caution.
6. For an inoperative switch failed to the off state, autothrottle functionality is
available in flight for the operative autothrottle.

Section 2 777 Dispatch Deviations Guide ATA 23
23-51-06 Microphone (MIC)/Interphone Switches
23-51-06-01 Control Wheel MIC/Interphone Switches
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 2 1 (M)
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated audio control panel MIC/interphone switch operates normally.
b. Affected switch is deactivated open.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the inoperative Control Wheel MIC/interphone switch, confirm it is
deactivated open and verify the associated pilot’s Audio Control Panel (ACP)
MIC/interphone switch operates normally (AMM 23-00-00/901).
1. Deactivate the inoperative control wheel MIC/interphone switch (AMM
23-51-06/401).
A. For Captain’s switch inoperative, open P11 panel
INTERPHONE-CAPTAIN circuit breaker.
B. For First Officer’s switch inoperative, open P11 panel
INTERPHONE-F/O circuit breaker.
C. Remove the two screws which mount the inoperative MIC/interphone
switch to the control wheel.
D. Pull the inoperative MIC/interphone switch out of the control wheel.
E. Disconnect, cap and stow the wires from the inoperative
MIC/interphone switch.
F. Install the associated MIC/interphone switch in the control wheel and
secure with the two screws.
G. For Captain’s switch inoperative, close P11 panel
INTERPHONE-CAPTAIN circuit breaker.
H. For First Officer’s switch inoperative, close P11 panel
INTERPHONE-F/O circuit breaker.
2. Confirm the inoperative Control Wheel MIC/interphone switch is
deactivated open and verify the associated pilot’s ACP MIC/interphone
switch operates normally.
A. Provide electrical power on the airplane (AMM 24-22-00/201).
B. Push the FLT Transmitter Select Switch on the Captain’s and F/O’s
ACPs and ensure the FLT MIC light is illuminated on both panels.
C. Ensure the FLT Receiver Light is illuminated and Receiver Volume
Control is properly adjusted on both ACPs.
D. Speak into the associated pilot’s microphone while simultaneously
pushing the deactivated Control Wheel MIC/interphone switch. No
transmission should be heard on the other pilot’s headset.

INBOARD DSPL selector (L INBD or R INBD).

associated inboard display unit.
2) Use the EFIS Control Panel to adjust the range and modes on
the ND to confirm the associated inboard display unit is properly
responding to the EFIS CONTROL PANEL.
D. On the DSP, one at a time, select the COMM and CHKL, and at least
two synoptic formats. As each DSP selection is made, ensure the
selected format appears on the associated inboard display unit.

System)
Interval Installed Required Procedure

MAINTENANCE (M)

the standby airspeed indicator system. An inoperative Standby Pitot
ADM (ARINC 429) results in a display flag on the standby airspeed
indicator.

34-00-00/901).

alignment. The Standby Attitude indicator should display sky/ground (blue
over brown) shading.

in).
3. Verify the ALTN ATTITUDE advisory message is displayed.
4. Verify the attitude sky/ground (blue over brown) shading and pitch scale is
displayed on both Primary Flight Displays (PFD) and no airspeed or
altitude failure flags are displayed on the Captain’s PFD.
5. Position both AIR DATA/ATT switches off (normal position - switch out).
6. Verify the ALTN ATTITUDE advisory message is not displayed.
OPERATIONS NOTE
Altitude differences may be noted between the standby altimeter display and the
primary displays, particularly at higher speeds and altitudes. The standby
altimeter defaults to a zero static source error correction when the standby
airspeed display is inoperative.

ATA 35 777 Dispatch Deviations Guide Section 2
OPERATIONS (O)
14 CFR passenger oxygen requirements (14 CFR 121.333(e)(1-3) vary with the
cruise altitude, the cabin pressure altitude to which an airplane may descend in
the event of a depressurization during the flight, and the time required to make the
emergency descent. If the airplane is operated at FL 250 or below and is able to
descend to 14,000 feet cabin pressure altitude or below within four minutes
following depressurization, oxygen must be available for 10% of passenger cabin
occupants for 30 minutes.
If the airplane is operated at or below FL 250 and is unable to descend to 14,000
or below within four minutes, or if the airplane is operated above FL 250
regardless of the time to descend to 14,000 feet cabin pressure altitude or below
following depressurization, oxygen must be available for 10% of the passenger
cabin occupants for the duration of the flight with cabin pressure altitudes above
10,000 feet and at or below 14,000 feet, except that there must not be less than a
10-minute supply for the passenger cabin occupants.
If the airplane is able to descend to between 14,000 and 15,000 feet cabin
pressure altitude, sufficient oxygen must be available for 30% of passenger cabin
occupants. If the airplane cannot descend below 15,000 feet cabin pressure
altitude, oxygen must be available for all (100%) of the passenger cabin
occupants. In these cases, oxygen must be available for the required number of
passengers for the entire duration of the flight flown at the cabin pressure
altitudes above 14,000 feet. In all cases, sufficient oxygen must be available for
the required number of passengers for at least 10 minutes. Operators should
check the appropriate regulations to ensure compliance.
For flights above flight level 250, an undiluted oxygen supply is required for no
less than two percent of the passengers for that portion of the flight at cabin
pressure altitudes above 8,000 feet following depressurization. In no case will the
supply be less than that required for one person.

49-15-01B APU Required
Interval Installed Required Procedure

May be inoperative provided:
a. Door is deactivated in the full open position.
b. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the door in the fully open position (AMM 49-00-00/901).
1. Position APU selector on the P5 overhead panel ON.
2. Wait 45 seconds then open and collar the P310 Panel APU INLET DR
ACTR circuit breaker.
3. Position APU selector on the P5 overhead panel OFF.
4. On the APU Maintenance page, confirm INLET DOOR POSITION
indicates OPEN.
A. If door is confirmed open, the door is deactivated in the fully open
position and no additional steps are required.
B. If door is not confirmed open, the following steps must be
accomplished to manually position and deactivate the door in the fully
open position:
5. Open the P49 Panel APUC 2 circuit breaker.
6. Open the P310 Panel DC FUEL PUMP and APUC 1 circuit breakers.
7. For APU oil heater installed, open the P320 Panel APU OIL HTR ASSY
circuit breaker. For APU oil heater not installed, the P320 panel APU OIL
HTR ASSY circuit breaker is inoperative and should remain open.
8. Open left and right APU Access Doors (315AL and 316AR).
9. Remove access cover from the inlet door actuator assembly.
10. Turn the transfer cover socket on the inlet door actuator counterclockwise
until MAN shows in the window of the transfer socket. The manual drive
socket will show. DO NOT apply more than 10 lb-in (1.1 N-m) of torque on
the transfer cover socket.
11. Turn the manual drive socket counter-clockwise until the torque value
suddenly increases. DO NOT apply more than 65 lb-in (7.3 N-m) of torque
on the manual drive socket.
12. Turn the transfer cover socket clockwise until ELEC shows in the forward
window of the transfer cover.
13. Re-install access cover on the inlet door actuator assembly.
14. Close left and right APU access doors.
15. Close the P49 Panel APUC 2 circuit breaker.

49-42-01 APU Starting System (Includes Electric Starter)
49-42-01A APU Required
Interval Installed Required Procedure
C 1 0 (O)
May be dispatched with APU START SYS faults provided APU is started before
departure and operated continuously throughout the flight.
MAINTENANCE NOTE
Some electric starter failures may result in damage to the APU if it is used. If the
APU fails to start electrically but starts pneumatically, the possibility of APU
damage can be reduced by doing the following steps.
1. Perform the APU Magnetic Chip Collector Inspection (AMM Task
49-27-04/201).
2. If the Chip Collector Inspection is satisfactory:
A. Position Overhead Maintenance Panel (P61) APU Maintenance
switch NORM.
B. Position Overhead Panel (P5) APU selector OFF.
C. Remove the end cap from the electric starter motor on the APU.
D. Use a socket and ratchet on the shaft for the electric starter to turn
the APU counterclockwise, facing aft.
1) The APU should turn freely. Verify the APU is turning freely by
visual inspection of the power section compressor blades
through the bottom access panel of the APU inlet duct (AMM
49-21-00/Figure 601).
2) If the APU does not turn freely, serious damage can occur if the
APU is operated (see FIM Chapter 49-40, Task 812, Fault
Isolation Procedure - Mechanical Fault).
E. Remove the socket and ratchet, and re-install the end cap on the
electric starter.
OPERATIONS (O)
1. Increase flight planning fuel by 2.5% to account for the open APU air inlet
door. Also increase flight planning fuel by 200 lb (90 kg) per hour of APU
usage in-flight and 535 lb (240 kg) per hour of APU usage on the ground.
2. Start the APU before departure and operate the APU continuously
throughout the flight.

Interval Installed Required Procedure

May be inoperative provided:
a. Door automatic locking electric solenoid is deactivated in the extended
position.
b. Door is verified to lock and unlock manually.
MAINTENANCE (M)
Deactivate the flight deck door automatic lock electric solenoid in the extended
position and verify the door locks and unlocks manually (AMM 52-00-00/901).
1. Open and collar P110 panel circuit breaker F/D DR LOCK.
2. Open the flight deck door and gain access to the door post.
3. Remove the seal assembly to get access to the screws that attach the
cover assembly to the door post (AMM 52-51-02/401).
4. Remove the cover assembly and strike assembly from the door post.
5. Use a strap or lockwire to hold the solenoid pin in the fully extended
position so that it holds the door catch in the locked position.
6. Install the cover and strike assemblies on the door post.
7. Install the seal assembly.
8. Close the flight deck door and verify that it is locked. Ensure a flight deck
door key is available or someone is in the flight deck before closing the
door.
9. Verify that the flight door unlocks from the cabin side with a key and from
the flight deck side with the door handle.

MAINTENANCE (M)
Lock the inoperative air/oil heat exchanger valve in the open position (AMM
79-00-00/901).
1. Gain access to the air/oil heat exchanger valve, which is located behind
and below the engine oil tank, by opening the right fan cowl panel on the
associated engine (AMM 71-11-04/201).
2. Lock the air/oil heat exchanger in the open position.
A. For RR engines not incorporating RR SB 79-C620.
1) Remove the cotter pin from the lockpin on the air/oil heat
exchanger valve.
2) Pull the lockpin out and remove the lockpin spacer (retain
spacer for restoration).
3) Turn the manual turning device in the clockwise direction until
valve is fully open and hold in this position until the lockpin has
been installed (Use caution as the valve is heavily spring
loaded).
4) Install the lockpin (without spacer) and release the manual
turning device.
5) Install the cotter pin through the upper hole in the lockpin.

opening the associated engine center thrust reverser latch access door
(415MB for left engine or 425MB right engine).

tube and into the manual override receptacle.

4. Upon command from the flight crew, use the starter drive extension to turn
the starter air valve to the open position and hold. Wear goggles, gloves
and protective clothing.

6. When the manual override start is complete, remove the starter drive
extension from the guide tube and close the center thrust reverser latch
access door.

associated engine center thrust reverser latch access panel (415JB for left
engine or 425JB right engine).

4. Upon command from the flight crew, engage the starter air valve manual
control handle, turn the starter air valve to the open position (clockwise -
one and one-quarter turns) and hold. Wear goggles, gloves and protective
clothing.
5. Upon command from the flight crew, close the starter air valve.
6. When the manual override start is complete, stow the starter air valve
manual control handle and close the center thrust reverser latch access
panel.

General Notes
This section contains locations, illustrations and performance information
for all of the CDL items from the 777 Airplane Flight Manual (AFM)
Appendix Configuration Deviation List (CDL) Revision 5.
Limitations
The associated limitations must be listed on a placard affixed in the
cockpit in clear view of the pilot-in-command and other appropriate crew
members.
Operation with those missing parts requiring a reduction of VMO/MMO is
permitted only when the airplane has the maximum airspeed limit
indication and the Mach airspeed warning system programmed for the
altitude/speed schedule specified for the applicable missing part.
The pilot in command will be notified of each operation with a missing
parts by listing the missing parts in the flight or dispatch release.
The operator will list in the aircraft logbook an appropriate notation
covering the missing parts on each flight.
If an additional part is lost in flight the airplane may not depart the airport
at which it landed following this event until it again complies with CDL
limitations. This, does not preclude the issuance of a ferry permit to allow
the airplane to be flown to a point where the necessary repairs or
replacements can be made.
Unless otherwise specified, combinations of parts from any system or
sub-systems may be missing. Combinations of parts from systems or
sub-systems that are not allowed will be specifically listed in the CDL.
Weight Reductions
The performance penalties are cumulative unless specifically designated
penalties for combination of missing parts are indicated. Where
performance penalties are listed as negligible, no more than three
negligible items may be missing without taking further penalty. For each
missing item more than three, reduce the takeoff, landing and enroute
climb limits by 100 pounds (46 kilograms). Where performance penalties
are listed as no penalty, any accumulative number of items listed as no
penalty may be missing without further penalty.

Enroute Diversion Speed Effects
The enroute climb weight penalties listed are based on operating speeds
that approximate the maximum lift-to-drag ratio speed. To account for the
difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the
enroute climb weight penalty listed by the following appropriate factor:

Enroute Fuel Mileage Effects
The drag effects of many 777 CDL items are so small that the changes in
flight planning fuel are negligible. For items that have enroute climb
weight penalties listed, an increase in flight planning fuel of 0.25% per
1,000 lb (454 kg) of enroute climb weight penalty (non-factored penalty)
may be used to account for the drag increase.

Airplane Model Information
Where applicable, airplane model information (annotation) is included
above affected text to identify configuration-specific information. The
annotation applies only to text aligned immediately below it and any
associated indented text. The following example illustrates the model
applicability for a Maintenance procedure:
MAINTENANCE (M)
Verify that the associated engine fuel shutoff valve is operating normally
once each flight day (AMM 73-00-00/901).
For PW:
1. If MAT is available, confirm that both maintenance messages are displayed
for the associated status message.
A. For status message ENG FUEL VALVE L, 73-40231 and 73-50231.
B. For status message ENG FUEL VALVE R, 73-40232 and 73-50232.
2. Start the associated engine and allow engine to stabilize at ground idle
(AMM 71-00-00/201).
3. Open the P11 panel FUEL SPAR VALVE circuit breaker for the associated
engine.
4. After minimum engine operating time, position the associated engine FUEL
CONTROL switch to CUTOFF and confirm engine shutdown.
5. For engine not shutdown, the fuel shutoff valve is not operating normally.
A. Monitor EGT and be prepared to motor the engine.
B. Close the P11 panel FUEL SPAR VALVE circuit breaker.
For PW or RR:
C. The engine may continue to operate for one minute.
For GE:
D. The engine may continue to operate for 10 seconds.
6. Confirm the associated FUEL SPAR VALVE L or R status message is
displayed.
7. Erase the latched FUEL SPAR VALVE L or R status message
(AMM 31-61-00/201).
8. After engine has stopped rotating, close the P11 panel FUEL SPAR VALVE
circuit breaker.
For the above example procedure, the applicable steps are as follows:
• For PW, steps 1, 1.A, 1.B, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5.A, 5.B, 5.C, 6 ,7 and 8 apply.
• For RR, steps 2, 3, 4, 5, 5.A, 5.B, 5.C, 6 ,7 and 8 apply.
• For GE, steps 2, 3, 4, 5, 5.A, 5.B, 5.D, 6 ,7 and 8 apply.

Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Information
Applying dispatch relief for the following items may affect the ability of the
airplane to meet the operational capabilities required for PBN operations.
The following information lists items that, if inoperative, may affect the
ability of the airplane to meet the performance and functional criteria for
various PBN operations. This information can aid in identifying potentially
affected capabilities associated with a particular dispatch configuration.
This section lists equipment requirements that may be found in the
document 777 RNP Navigation Capabilities Document D243W018-13,
revision "M" (or later). Operators should consult their Operations
Specification for requirements applicable to their operations.
PBN Equipment Requirements
Two Primary Flight Displays (PFD) and Navigation
Displays (ND) - (31-61-01)
All PBN operations require two PFDs with mini map.
The 777 is equipped with six display units. The PFDs are normally
displayed on the outboard display units and the NDs are normally
displayed on the inboard display units. Dispatch is only allowed with the
lower center display unit inoperative. Therefore, this requirement will
always be met for dispatch.
Two Control Display Units (CDU) - (34-61-03)
All PBN operations require two CDUs.
The 777 is equipped with three CDUs. Dispatch is allowed with the center
DCU inoperative. Both left and right CDUs must operate normally for
dispatch. Therefore, this requirement will always be met for dispatch.
AIMS Operational Software
For RNP AR APCH and RNP APCH:
Airplane must be equiped with AIMS BP05A or later. Navigation
Performance Scales and LNAV Go-Around Auto-Engage must be
enabled.
Airplanes without Navigation Performance Scales and LNAV Go-Around
Auto-Engage (AIMS BP03 and earlier versions) do not support these
operations.

Therefore, this requirement will always be met for dispatch.
Autopilot Flight Director Computers (AFDC) - (22-11-01)
RNP AR APCH operations require two AFDCs to operate normally. All
other PBN operations require a single operational AFDC.
The 777 is equipped with three AFDCs. MMEL dispatch is allowed with
one, two, or all three AFDCs inoperative. Therefore, PBN operations may
be affected with more than one AFDC inoperative.
PBN operations may be allowed using either the autopilot function or
flight director function.
Mode Control Panel (MCP) Switches - (22-11-06)
The following equipment must operate normally in order to use the
autoplot function and flight director function:
Approach (APP) Mode Control Panel (MCP) switch must operate
normally for RNP AR APCH and RNP APCH.
Lateral navigation (LNAV) Mode Control Panel (MCP) switch must
operate normally for all PBN operations.
Vertical navigation (VNAV) Mode Control Panel (MCP) switch must
operate normally for RNP AR APCH operations. Other vertical modes
may be used for other PBN operations.
Autopilot Function
If the autopilot function is inoperative, PBN operations may be allowed
using only the flight director function.
The autopilot function may not be used if any of the following equipment
is inoperative:
1. Both autopilot engage switches. (22-11-06)
2. One control wheel autopilot disconnect switch below 1500 feet
AGL. (22-11-08)
3. Both control wheel autopilot disconnect switches inoperative.
(22-11-08)
4. Warning Electronic System (WES) Autopilot disconnect warning
function. (31-51-05)

Section 4 777 Dispatch Deviations Guide General
Flight Director Systems (22-11-10)
If the flight director function is inoperative, PBN operations may be
allowed using only the autopilot function.
The flight director function is considered inoperative if any of the following
equipment is inoperative:
1. One or more Flight Director Systems (22-11-10).
2. One or more Mode Control Panel (MCP) Flight Director (F/D)
switches. (22-11-06)
Both flight director display functions are required for RNP AR APCH.
Flight director function for pilot flying (PF) is required for RNP APCH.
Takeoff/Go-Around (TO/GA) Switches (22-11-09)
There are two TO/GA switches are installed on the 777. MMEL dispatch
is allowed with one or both TO/GA switches inoperative.
For RNP AR APCH, both TO/GA switches must operate normally.
For both TO/GA switches inoperative, PBN operations that require either
autopilot or flight director use below 500 feet AGL or MDA, whichever is
higher, may not be used. RNP AR APCH, RNP APCH, RNP 1, P-RNAV,
RNAV 1 and Advanced RNP operations may not be allowed.
VOR Navigation Systems (34-51-01)
The 777 is equipped with two VORs. For dispatch, either one or both
VORs may be inoperative.
• When dispatching with a single GPS system, RNP APCH, RNP 1/RNP
2, and Advanced RNP operations are allowed provided provided at
least one of the following operates normally: GPS, VOR or DME.
Global Positioning Systems (GPS) (34-58-01)
The 777 is equipped with two GPSs. For dispatch, either one or both
GPSs may be inoperative.

Introduction
The Dispatch Deviations Guide (DDG) is intended to assist airline operations and maintenance
organizations in developing the procedures required to operate the airplane in the various
nonstandard configurations authorized by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Master
Minimum Equipment List (MMEL) and the Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) Appendix
Configuration Deviation List (CDL). The DDG is used as a reference by operators to develop
their Minimum Equipment List (MEL) and is not a regulatory-approved document.
A DDG is typically revised when the associated model’s FAA MMEL is updated by a standard
revision. At Boeing’s discretion, updated procedural guidance information may be made
available via a DDG Supplement prior to a complete DDG revision. A DDG Supplement is only
effective for its associated DDG revision.
A DDG Supplement is identified by its associated DDG revision number followed by a dash,
then a sequential number. An individual DDG Supplement may be superseded by a newer DDG
Supplement. In addition, if Boeing subsequently releases a new DDG revision, then previous
DDG Supplements will be incorporated into that DDG revision. The DDG Supplement Record
below will be retained for historical reference. DDG Supplement Status may be ‘Active’,
‘Superseded’, or ‘Incorporated’. Only ‘Active’ DDG Supplements are contained herein.
